newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-lower Thursday.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-lower Thursday.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs were expected to be steady to $0.50 per cwt lower on Thursday with the market beginning to stabilize after its recent slide, livestock dealers said.
"They are talking like it may be bottoming out pretty soon but we should get a decent run again tomorrow," one Indiana dealer said.

Prices have been sliding for more than a week with cooler weather in much of the U.S. Midwest prompting a pick-up in runs. Demand has also been waning with IBP announcing this week it was cutting production at all its Midwest pork plants.
USDA reported a top in Iowa-south Minnesota on Wednesday of $57.50 per cwt, down $0.50 on the day and a drop of $4.00 since July 22.
"I think it should steady back up but I don't think there will be any strength to it," one Ohio based dealer said.
Dealers noted hog weights were falling slightly, although they remained above year ago levels.
USDA reported an average hog weight in Iowa-south Minnesota for the week to July 26 of 250 lbs, down from 250.9 lbs a week earlier but up from 244.8 lbs in the same week a year ago.
